target: हम सात लोग एक साथ रहते हैं।
english: The seven of us live together.
reason: "मेरे परिवार के सात लोग" is translationese – nobody uses a genitive to count their household; Hindi says "हम सात लोग" or "परिवार में सात लोग हैं". Same node-05 counting pattern, same length, same vocabulary, and phrased the way it is actually said.

english: Today is the twentieth of March.
reason: "आज तारीख़ बीस मार्च है" is ungrammatical-sounding – it needs "आज की तारीख़" or, far more commonly, no तारीख़ at all. Spoken Hindi just states the date. Same node-05 date pattern, same vocabulary.

target: क्या यह पानी पीने लायक़ है?
english: Is this water safe to drink?
reason: "पीने योग्य" is bureaucratic/signboard register (everyday speech uses "पीने लायक़"), and "और साफ़" is padding that adds nothing. Same node-03 yes/no question about water, same length, natural spoken wording.

target: मेरा नया बैग बहुत हल्का है।
english: My new bag is very light.
reason: Padded and tautological – "अच्छा और सुहावना" says the same thing twice, and the card is a near-duplicate of hi-0529 ("नमस्ते, आज मौसम बहुत अच्छा है"). Replacement keeps the node-07 possessive + adjective + है pattern with everyday vocabulary.

target: खाने को थोड़ा और गरम कर दो।
english: Heat the food up a bit more.
reason: "हरी मिर्च खाने को तीखा बनाती है" is a textbook fact a learner would never say, and the verb is off (natural Hindi would be "तीखा कर देती है"). Replacement keeps the node-06 "खाने को" object-marker pattern in a sentence people actually use at the table.

target: मैं और मेरा भाई साथ पढ़ते हैं।
english: My brother and I study together.
reason: "भाई और मैं" copies English word order and drops the possessive – Hindi says "मैं और मेरा भाई"; "साथ मिलकर" is also redundant. Same node-01 family + habitual pattern, same length and vocabulary.

target: वह हमेशा देर से आता है।
reason: "वह हमेशा सच बोलता है" is a moral-education copybook line, not something a learner will ever need. Replacement keeps the node-02 habitual present with हमेशा but says something people genuinely complain about.
